newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda reopens bidding for coffee marketing board.
newsitem.headline: Uganda reopens bidding for coffee marketing board.

text.p: The Ugandan government has called for fresh bids for 51 percent of its shareholding in the Coffee Marketing Board Limited (CMBL) after it rejected as unacceptable a sole bid by Swiss company Sucafina.
In a report dated April 1 but sent to Reuters on Tuesday, CMBL privatisation coordinator William Okecho said talks to get Sucafina to raise an original bid of $3.3 million had failed.

"Following talks with Sucafina, we have not been able to successfully complete the sale of CMBL because Sucafina has failed to meet government expectations. Sucafina SA has confirmed this in writing," Okecho said.

Okecho said fresh advertisements for interested core investors in CMBL would be posted this month. He urged all interested parties to submit their proposals to the privatisation unit and promised a speedy decision.
On March 19, a consortium of five Ugandan companies urged the government to re-open bidding for the CMBL but at the time the minister responsible said that would be unfair.
Under the umbrella Uganda Consortium of Agro-Processors (AGACAP), the companies placed a new bid of $5.5 million.

At the time AGACAP Chairman Jamada Lutta Musoke told reporters it was unwise to sell a strategic concern such as the board to foreign buyers and said Sucafina would be welcomed into the new consortium if it made a formal request.

But Minister of state for privatisation Matthew Rukikaire said Sucafina was the only company that showed interest when the government called for bids for the board two years ago and it would be unfair to re-open bidding.
He was not immediately available to comment on Tuesday.
Okecho said the consortium would have to tranform itself into a company to qualify to tender.
In December, the Ugandan government rejected a $3.3 million Sucafina bid for 51 percent of the CMBL.

CMBL assets included in that sale were valued at $36.7 million. The company's principal asset is its processing and storage unit in Bugoolobi. It has an export processing capacity of four million 60-kg bags a year.

Previously, Ugandan privatisation officials have said that a bidder who offered two-thirds of the value price would be considered serious but if one was not found then they would be comfortable selling at a lower price only to Ugandan investors.

Geneva-based Sucafina was the only bidder for the CMBL stake, submitting its bid two minutes before the deadline on September 26. It had offered to buy the 51 percent stake in two tranches, one of $1.8 million and a second of $1.5 million.
CMBL's market share in the coffee export business fell to 9.4 percent in 1995, compared with around 84 percent four years earlier.
Uganda has more than 100 private coffee exporters.
